question: Why did only some of the Northgate invoices land in the wrong month, not all of them?
gold: Dates with a day of 13 or more can't be read month-first, so dateutil fell back to day-first and got them right; only invoices dated on days 1 to 12 had day and month swapped.

The wrong-month invoice date bug in copperline-docs is Northgate-only; it does not affect invoices from other carriers.
The Northgate wrong-month bug only affects invoices dated on days 1 through 12 of a month, because dates with day 13 or later cannot be read as a month and dateutil falls back to day-first for them.
The Northgate wrong-month invoice bug matters because Rosebud posts an invoice to the accounting period matching its invoice date, so a wrong month means the invoice is posted to the wrong accounting period.

answer: Northgate writes invoice dates day-first, so `04/03/2026` means 4 March. `parse_date` in `fields.py` uses dateutil's default, which reads the first number as the month, so that date became April 3. This only happens when the day is 1 through 12. For day 13 or later, the first number can't be a month, so dateutil falls back to day-first and gets it right. That's why NG-20260317-311 came out correct while NG-20260304-118 didn't.
judge_reason: The answer correctly explains that only days 1–12 were ambiguous and swapped, while days 13 or later forced dateutil to interpret the dates day-first.

question: Why were Northgate Haulage invoice dates coming out wrong in copperline-docs?
gold: Northgate prints dates day-first (DD/MM/YYYY) and the parser read them month-first with dateutil's default, so an invoice dated 04/03/2026 (4 March) became April 3.

Northgate Haulage prints day-first dates, so 04/03/2026 means 4 March. The copperline extractor parsed them with dateutil, which reads them month-first. Invoices dated on days 1–12 therefore landed in the wrong month, and some came out as April or November. Invoices on days 13 and up, like NG-20260317-311, parsed correctly because they can't be read month-first.

The fix on 2026-09-16 (#8, closing #7) has each carrier declare a `date_format` in `config/carriers.yaml`. Northgate uses `%d/%m/%Y`, and parsing now uses `strptime`. Northgate also now carries `currency: CAD`.
judge_reason: The answer correctly identifies Northgate’s day-first date format and dateutil’s month-first default as the cause, including the March 4 versus April 3 ambiguity, and its additional details do not contradict the reference.

gold: In config/carriers.yaml: each carrier has a date_format ("%d/%m/%Y" for Northgate), and dates are parsed with datetime.strptime, so a mismatch fails instead of guessing.

# Copperline kickoff call

With Theo Brandt (ops) and Lupe Herrera (AP specialist, does the keying today).

## Today
- Lupe keys every invoice into Rosebud TMS by hand: about 6 minutes per invoice, more for multi-stop loads.
- ~600 carrier invoices a month. Spikes at month end.
- Rosebud import screen takes a CSV, one row per invoice. Lupe will send the import template.

## Fields they need
carrier, invoice number, invoice date, PRO number, BOL number, origin zip, destination zip, weight, line haul,
fuel surcharge, accessorials, total

## Notes
- Northgate Haulage is in Winnipeg and bills in Canadian dollars. Rosebud has a currency column.
- Ridgeway sends scans. Out of phase 1.
- Bugs and data problems go in GitHub issues on the repo (Theo has a GitHub account). Business stuff by email.
- Weekly check-in Thursdays at 10:00, 20 min, video.

answer:
Bluestem BOLs repeat the line-item header row at the top of page 2. `line_items` in `src/copperline/extract/tables.py` only accepted exactly one table, so any multi-page BOL returned nothing. The two-page sample `BS-BOL-558201.pdf` showed this: 14 rows on page 1, 9 on page 2, and 0 merged.

The fix, in the 2026-09-14 commit "extract: join Bluestem BOL tables across pages", joins the per-page tables when their header rows match and drops the repeated headers. It also sets `vertical_strategy: lines` for Bluestem, because its tables have ruled lines and the text strategy splits the description column in two.

The same commit also mapped the LFTG, RESI and INSD accessorial codes in `config/carriers.yaml` and added `tests/test_bluestem.py`.

Day 14:
"Hi Jordan, invoice 1043 is two weeks past due. Can you tell me the date it will be paid? I will pause new work until I have a date."

Notice the pattern. Each message names the invoice, names one next step, and offers a way out that is not a confrontation. Readers who switched to this sequence told us roughly a third of their "late" invoices were paid within a day of the first message.

2. READER QUESTION

"One client pays all vendors in a single batch on the 20th. Should I time my invoices to land just before it?"

Yes. Ask their accounts payable contact for the batch calendar once, then put the cutoff in your own calendar. A twelve-minute email now saves a month of waiting every time you miss the window by a day.

3. WORTH YOUR TIME
Takeaway for small carriers: the paperwork is the claim. If the in-time is not on a document, the invoice will be negotiated.

PAPERWORK WATCH

Invoice mismatches remain the top reason for slow payment between carriers and shippers. The usual suspects are a rate confirmation that says one thing and an invoice that says another, a fuel surcharge figured on the wrong week's index, and lumper receipts that never made it into the packet. Several mid-size shippers now reject invoices automatically when the load number on the PDF does not match their TMS.

Meanwhile, more carriers are trying OCR to read invoices and bills of lading. Accuracy on clean scans is above 95 percent in vendor demos. On documents that were faxed and then scanned, nobody wants to quote a number.

- Tamarack Line Haul named a new CFO after eight months with the seat empty.
- The port at Savannah reported its busiest August on record.
- Redfern Freight is acquiring Alder & Cole Logistics, terms undisclosed.

# Copperline check-in

Theo, Lupe, me.

- Northgate dates fixed (#8). Lupe re-ran March, all good.
- Bluestem two-page BOLs work now.

  those instead of everything. Agreed, doing it this week.
- Next week: Rosebud template + export.
4. Rate drift, where the invoiced linehaul does not match the contracted lane rate.
5. Weight or class corrections applied after the fact with no reweigh ticket.

THE DOCUMENT PROBLEM

Almost every audit stalls on the same thing. The invoice is a PDF, the bill of lading is a different PDF, the rate confirmation is an email, and the TMS record holds a fourth version. Someone has to line up four sources by hand. A logistics manager at a Texas shipper told us her team spends about two days a month on exactly this.

Software vendors are circling the problem. Most pitches combine OCR with field extraction and a match against the TMS. The ones that survive a pilot tend to do one boring thing well, such as pulling the load number, carrier name, invoice total and ship date into a clean row, and flagging what they could not read.

NUMBERS TO KNOW

- Average days to pay a carrier invoice (reported): 38
- Share of invoices needing one or more corrections: 14 percent
- Share of audits that found duplicate payments: 41 percent

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.

- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

## Open
- [ ] fall menu with item codes (Dana, next week)
- [ ] texting number

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

## Open
- [ ] fall menu with item codes (Dana, next week)
- [ ] texting number

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

## Open
- [ ] fall menu with item codes (Dana, next week)
- [ ] texting number

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.

  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.

- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

## Open
- [ ] fall menu with item codes (Dana, next week)
- [ ] texting number

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

## Open
- [ ] fall menu with item codes (Dana, next week)
- [ ] texting number

# Fernbrook text ordering: spec

From the call with Dana, Sep 3.

## Locations
- Old Town (main kitchen, bakes for Eastgate)
- Eastgate
- Riverside

## Rules
- Next-day pickup orders must come in by **2pm** the day before.
- Max **6 dozen** per text order. Bigger orders: reply asking them to call the store.
- Customer says which location. If they don't, ask.
- **Never text customers before 8am.** Their old ordering service sent confirmations at 5am when the bakers
  started and people complained. Bakers start at 4.
- Payment at pickup only. No online payment in v1.

## Kitchen sheet
- Google Sheet, one tab per location.
- Columns: pickup date, pickup time, name, phone, items, total, notes.
- A **Needs a human** tab for anything the parser isn't sure about. Dana or a manager checks it at 7am and 1pm.

## Open
- [ ] fall menu with item codes (Dana, next week)
- [ ] texting number

# Harbor Lane discovery call

Marisol Ortega (office manager), Dr. Evan Kim (owner, approves budget).

## Their setup
- Practice software: **ChairSide**. No API. It can write a nightly CSV export at **11pm** to a shared folder:
  `\\HL-SERVER\exports\appts_YYYYMMDD.csv`
- Columns: patient id, first name, last name, mobile, appt date, appt time, provider, location, TXT_OK
- `TXT_OK` is the patient's opt-in to texts. Only text patients with TXT_OK = Y.

## Rules
- HIPAA: the texting vendor has to sign a BAA before any real patient data goes through it.
- Texts carry **only** the first name, the appointment date and time, and the location. No procedure, no provider
  notes, nothing clinical.
- Reminders + a no-show follow-up with a link to rebook.

## Timeline
- Go-live target: **Thursday October 15**.

# Harbor Lane discovery call

Marisol Ortega (office manager), Dr. Evan Kim (owner, approves budget).

## Their setup
- Practice software: **ChairSide**. No API. It can write a nightly CSV export at **11pm** to a shared folder:
  `\\HL-SERVER\exports\appts_YYYYMMDD.csv`
- Columns: patient id, first name, last name, mobile, appt date, appt time, provider, location, TXT_OK
- `TXT_OK` is the patient's opt-in to texts. Only text patients with TXT_OK = Y.

## Rules
- HIPAA: the texting vendor has to sign a BAA before any real patient data goes through it.
- Texts carry **only** the first name, the appointment date and time, and the location. No procedure, no provider
  notes, nothing clinical.
- Reminders + a no-show follow-up with a link to rebook.

## Timeline
- Go-live target: **Thursday October 15**.

The file is also Windows-1252 (cp1252), not UTF-8, which is why the Codex session switched the importer to `encoding="cp1252"`.

# Harbor Lane discovery call

Marisol Ortega (office manager), Dr. Evan Kim (owner, approves budget).

## Their setup
- Practice software: **ChairSide**. No API. It can write a nightly CSV export at **11pm** to a shared folder:
  `\\HL-SERVER\exports\appts_YYYYMMDD.csv`
- Columns: patient id, first name, last name, mobile, appt date, appt time, provider, location, TXT_OK
- `TXT_OK` is the patient's opt-in to texts. Only text patients with TXT_OK = Y.

## Rules
- HIPAA: the texting vendor has to sign a BAA before any real patient data goes through it.
- Texts carry **only** the first name, the appointment date and time, and the location. No procedure, no provider
  notes, nothing clinical.
- Reminders + a no-show follow-up with a link to rebook.

## Timeline
- Go-live target: **Thursday October 15**.

# Harbor Lane discovery call

Marisol Ortega (office manager), Dr. Evan Kim (owner, approves budget).

## Their setup
- Practice software: **ChairSide**. No API. It can write a nightly CSV export at **11pm** to a shared folder:
  `\\HL-SERVER\exports\appts_YYYYMMDD.csv`
- Columns: patient id, first name, last name, mobile, appt date, appt time, provider, location, TXT_OK
- `TXT_OK` is the patient's opt-in to texts. Only text patients with TXT_OK = Y.

## Rules
- HIPAA: the texting vendor has to sign a BAA before any real patient data goes through it.
- Texts carry **only** the first name, the appointment date and time, and the location. No procedure, no provider
  notes, nothing clinical.
- Reminders + a no-show follow-up with a link to rebook.

## Timeline
- Go-live target: **Thursday October 15**.
3. SAY WHO THE PATIENT IS. Parents get texts for several children. Put the child's first name in the message, or you will field a call that begins "which one?"

4. A SECOND TOUCH BEATS A BETTER FIRST ONE. Practices that sent a short follow-up to anyone who had not replied saw the biggest lift, more than any rewrite of the first message.

5. NEVER GO PAST THREE. Three touches in total was the ceiling before opt-outs climbed.

WHEN A PATIENT TEXTS BACK SOMETHING ODD

Sandpiper Orthodontics logged a month of replies. About 8 percent were not "yes" or "no": questions about parking, cost, whether a parent could bring a sibling, "wrong number." Their front desk now checks the reply inbox before each opening and again before close. Unanswered replies were the main source of one-star reviews.

TEMPLATE LIBRARY (members): https://recallletter.example/templates/reminders
Next webinar: Handling the angry no-show call. https://recallletter.example/webinars/angry-no-show

The Recall Letter team

# Quill & Ledger discovery

Ines Albright and Martin Hale (both partners). 2 staff bookkeepers.

- 140 clients, about **3,000 documents a month**, way more in January to April.
- Today: one shared Google Drive folder per client. Bookkeepers sort by hand, then categorize in QuickBooks Online.
- Ines is the champion. **Martin is skeptical** about AI touching client financial data. His condition: for the
  first month, a person approves every categorization before it goes into QuickBooks.
- Hard deadline: live before **January 15**, when tax season starts.
- Payroll: they want payroll exported into QuickBooks too.

Idea: an intake email address per client + a review queue. Categorize with an LLM against each client's chart of
accounts, show the suggestion, bookkeeper clicks approve.

Next: proposal by Friday.

# Harbor Lane discovery call

Marisol Ortega (office manager), Dr. Evan Kim (owner, approves budget).

## Their setup
- Practice software: **ChairSide**. No API. It can write a nightly CSV export at **11pm** to a shared folder:
  `\\HL-SERVER\exports\appts_YYYYMMDD.csv`
- Columns: patient id, first name, last name, mobile, appt date, appt time, provider, location, TXT_OK
- `TXT_OK` is the patient's opt-in to texts. Only text patients with TXT_OK = Y.

## Rules
- HIPAA: the texting vendor has to sign a BAA before any real patient data goes through it.
- Texts carry **only** the first name, the appointment date and time, and the location. No procedure, no provider
  notes, nothing clinical.
- Reminders + a no-show follow-up with a link to rebook.

## Timeline
- Go-live target: **Thursday October 15**.

All three misses are near misses between sibling accounts (Meals vs Client Meals, Software vs Subscriptions) or a judgment call (supplies for resale counted as cost of goods). Confidence was below 0.7 on two of the three, so a review queue that sorts low confidence first would put them in front of a bookkeeper. This supports the approval step Martin wants: in month 1 a person approves every suggestion, and the match rate on real documents tells them whether to keep doing that.
Takeaway for small carriers: the paperwork is the claim. If the in-time is not on a document, the invoice will be negotiated.

PAPERWORK WATCH

Invoice mismatches remain the top reason for slow payment between carriers and shippers. The usual suspects are a rate confirmation that says one thing and an invoice that says another, a fuel surcharge figured on the wrong week's index, and lumper receipts that never made it into the packet. Several mid-size shippers now reject invoices automatically when the load number on the PDF does not match their TMS.

Meanwhile, more carriers are trying OCR to read invoices and bills of lading. Accuracy on clean scans is above 95 percent in vendor demos. On documents that were faxed and then scanned, nobody wants to quote a number.

# Quill & Ledger discovery

Ines Albright and Martin Hale (both partners). 2 staff bookkeepers.

- 140 clients, about **3,000 documents a month**, way more in January to April.
- Today: one shared Google Drive folder per client. Bookkeepers sort by hand, then categorize in QuickBooks Online.
- Ines is the champion. **Martin is skeptical** about AI touching client financial data. His condition: for the
  first month, a person approves every categorization before it goes into QuickBooks.
- Hard deadline: live before **January 15**, when tax season starts.
- Payroll: they want payroll exported into QuickBooks too.

Idea: an intake email address per client + a review queue. Categorize with an LLM against each client's chart of
accounts, show the suggestion, bookkeeper clicks approve.

Next: proposal by Friday.

# Quill & Ledger discovery

Ines Albright and Martin Hale (both partners). 2 staff bookkeepers.

- 140 clients, about **3,000 documents a month**, way more in January to April.
- Today: one shared Google Drive folder per client. Bookkeepers sort by hand, then categorize in QuickBooks Online.
- Ines is the champion. **Martin is skeptical** about AI touching client financial data. His condition: for the
  first month, a person approves every categorization before it goes into QuickBooks.
- Hard deadline: live before **January 15**, when tax season starts.
- Payroll: they want payroll exported into QuickBooks too.

Idea: an intake email address per client + a review queue. Categorize with an LLM against each client's chart of
accounts, show the suggestion, bookkeeper clicks approve.

Next: proposal by Friday.

# Quill & Ledger discovery

Ines Albright and Martin Hale (both partners). 2 staff bookkeepers.

- 140 clients, about **3,000 documents a month**, way more in January to April.
- Today: one shared Google Drive folder per client. Bookkeepers sort by hand, then categorize in QuickBooks Online.
- Ines is the champion. **Martin is skeptical** about AI touching client financial data. His condition: for the
  first month, a person approves every categorization before it goes into QuickBooks.
- Hard deadline: live before **January 15**, when tax season starts.
- Payroll: they want payroll exported into QuickBooks too.

Idea: an intake email address per client + a review queue. Categorize with an LLM against each client's chart of
accounts, show the suggestion, bookkeeper clicks approve.

Next: proposal by Friday.

# Quill & Ledger discovery

Ines Albright and Martin Hale (both partners). 2 staff bookkeepers.

accounts, show the suggestion, bookkeeper clicks approve.

answer: Pinch 0.4.1 fixed it (PR #33, which closed issue #31). The bug was that paths from the user's environment were joined into a regex without escaping. On Windows, the backslashes in a path like `C:\Users\me\app\logs` were read as escape sequences. That caused a crash (`re.error: bad escape \U`) or redaction of the wrong text. The fix escapes paths with `re.escape` before they become patterns.
judge_reason: The answer correctly identifies version 0.4.1 and explains that unescaped Windows path backslashes were interpreted as regex escape sequences, fixed by using re.escape.

1. FASTAPI BACKGROUND TASKS VS A REAL QUEUE

Background tasks are great for "send the email after you return the response." They are risky for anything you cannot afford to lose, because they live and die with the worker process. A deploy in the middle of a task drops the task. The post draws the line clearly: if a lost job means a lost customer order, use a queue (even a database table with a status column and a polling worker). If a lost job means a missed analytics ping, background tasks are fine. https://walrusdigest.example/links/background-vs-queue

answer: A 401 Unauthorized means the request lacks valid authentication: no credentials, or bad or expired ones. The client can retry after authenticating, and the response usually carries a `WWW-Authenticate` header. A 403 Forbidden means the server knows who you are (or that identity doesn't matter) but won't allow the action, so logging in again won't help unless you have different permissions.

**Added to `git/.config/git/config`.** `git st` is `status -sb`. `git lg` is a one-line graph log with relative dates, authors and refs. `git cleanup` deletes local branches already merged into `main`.

**How `cleanup` stays safe.** It lists branches with `--merged main`, skips `main` and the current branch, and deletes with `-d`, so git refuses anything unmerged even if the filter were wrong.

**Checked.** I ran it on a scratch repository with a merged branch, an unmerged branch, the current branch and `main`. Only the merged one was deleted, and a second run with nothing to delete exited cleanly. The pager shows the colors because `LESS` contains `-R`. It only looks at local branches, so branches that were squash-merged on GitHub show as unmerged and stay until you remove them by hand.

Only do this on a commit you haven't pushed. If it's already pushed, use `git revert` instead.

# Sourdough loaf

## Starter
Feed 1:5:5 (starter, flour, water). Use it when it has doubled and just started to dome. If it has collapsed, it is late.

## Dough
- 500 g bread flour
- 350 g water
- 100 g active starter
- 10 g salt

## Method
1. Mix flour and water, rest 30 minutes (autolyse).
2. Add starter and salt. Fold every 30 minutes, four times.
3. Bulk until about 50 percent bigger. Shape. Fridge overnight.
4. Bake in a preheated Dutch oven, lid on, then lid off to finish.

## Notes
- Hydration is the lever. Too wet and the loaf spreads, too dry and it's dense.
- Underfed starter makes a brick. Learned that the hard way.

## Troubleshooting
- Dense crumb: starter was late or bulk was short.
- Gummy middle: cut it too soon. Wait an hour.
- Flat loaf: dough was too slack, add a fold or two next time.
- Pale crust: bake the second half with the lid off a little longer.

THE DAYLIGHT SAVING TRAP

Twice a year, "same time tomorrow" is not 24 hours later. If you add 24 hours to a timestamp instead of adding a day to a local date, you will be an hour off for a week. Clocks in most of the U.S. change on the first Sunday of November. Put it on your calendar now and test before it arrives.

THE FORMAT TRAP

03/04 is March 4th in the U.S. and the 3rd of April nearly everywhere else. If your inputs come from a form, use a date picker. If they come from text, ask for the month spelled out.

READER BUG OF THE MONTH

A tutoring business exported schedules to a spreadsheet and the date column silently turned into text on every row that began with a zero. The reminder script skipped them. Nobody noticed for nine days. The fix was one format setting and a check that counts rows processed against rows exported.

answer: A list is mutable, so you can add, remove, or change its items after you create it. A tuple is immutable, so its contents are fixed once created. That makes tuples hashable (when their items are) and usable as dict keys or set members, and they're often used for fixed groupings of values.

answer:
`set -euo pipefail` makes a bash script fail fast instead of carrying on after errors:

- **`-e`** exits the script as soon as a command returns a non-zero status.
- **`-u`** treats an unset variable as an error instead of expanding it to an empty string.
- **`-o pipefail`** makes a pipeline's exit status the first failing command's status, not just the last command's. Without it, `false | cat` counts as success.

One caveat from your dotfiles install.sh: in bash 3.2 (the macOS default), `-u` counts an empty array as unset. The script had to account for that.

answer: An idempotency key is a unique value (usually a UUID) that a client sends with a request, such as a payment charge. The server saves the result under that key. If the client sends the same request again, for example after a timeout or network retry, the server returns the saved result and doesn't run the operation a second time. This stops a retry from charging a customer twice.

## Docs
- Your staff already live in it. Adoption is a feature.
- You want a human to be able to fix a bad row with a click and an undo.

SIGNS YOU'RE OUTGROWING IT

1. Quota errors. If your script starts seeing "429 Quota exceeded for quota metric 'Read requests'", you are reading cell by cell. Batch the reads (one call for the whole range) before you decide anything else.
2. Two things write to the same row at once and the last writer wins. This one is subtle and shows up as "sometimes a number is wrong."
3. You have formulas that reference formulas that reference another file. One broken link and half the sheet turns to #REF!.
4. Somebody asks "can we see this by customer over the last two years?" and the answer takes an afternoon.

THE MOVE, WHEN YOU MAKE IT

You do not have to throw the sheet away. A common pattern: keep the sheet as the friendly face for staff, put Postgres underneath for anything that needs history or reporting, and sync one direction. The sheet shows; the database remembers.

answer: Use a frozen dataclass: `@dataclass(frozen=True)`. After that, assigning to a field raises `FrozenInstanceError`, and `__hash__` is generated, so instances can go in sets or be used as dict keys. If you also want less memory use and faster attribute access, add `slots=True` (Python 3.10+). Frozen only blocks reassigning fields. A mutable value inside, such as a list, can still be changed.

**Added to `git/.config/git/config`.** `git st` is `status -sb`. `git lg` is a one-line graph log with relative dates, authors and refs. `git cleanup` deletes local branches already merged into `main`.

**How `cleanup` stays safe.** It lists branches with `--merged main`, skips `main` and the current branch, and deletes with `-d`, so git refuses anything unmerged even if the filter were wrong.

**Checked.** I ran it on a scratch repository with a merged branch, an unmerged branch, the current branch and `main`. Only the merged one was deleted, and a second run with nothing to delete exited cleanly. The pager shows the colors because `LESS` contains `-R`. It only looks at local branches, so branches that were squash-merged on GitHub show as unmerged and stay until you remove them by hand.
answer: Try `unique_in_order`. It says the function removes duplicates and keeps the first occurrence of each item in its original order. Other good options are `dedupe_keep_order` and `ordered_unique`. If you want the Python-style name, `dedupe` is short, but it doesn't mention order. In Python, `list(dict.fromkeys(items))` does this in one line.

answer:
Both commands bring changes from one branch into another, but they do it differently.

**Merge** joins the two histories with a new merge commit. Nothing is rewritten, so the history shows exactly what happened, including the branching.

**Rebase** takes your commits and replays them on top of the other branch's latest commit. That makes the history a straight line, but your commits get new hashes. Don't rebase commits you've already shared.

Your dotfiles already set `pull.rebase = true`, so `git pull` rebases your local commits on top of upstream instead of creating merge commits.

THE RECALL LETTER
Issue 78

REMINDER TEXTS THAT GET REPLIES

We collected 31 reminder templates from member practices and read them all in one sitting. A few patterns separate the ones that get answered from the ones that get ignored.

1. THE PRACTICE NAME COMES FIRST. Patients get texts from numbers they do not know. "Lakemont Pediatric Dentistry: Ava's visit is Tuesday" gets read. "Reminder: appointment Tuesday" looks like spam.

2. ONE ASK PER MESSAGE. "Reply 1 to confirm or 2 to reschedule" outperformed templates that offered four options. Practices that offered a phone number as well saw more calls and fewer replies.

3. SAY WHO THE PATIENT IS. Parents get texts for several children. Put the child's first name in the message, or you will field a call that begins "which one?"
New: "Hi Maria, it's Cedar Row Dental. We have you down for Thursday afternoon. Tap here to confirm or pick a new time: [link]"

The second one asks for something specific and makes the easy answer one tap long.

# Harbor Lane discovery call

Marisol Ortega (office manager), Dr. Evan Kim (owner, approves budget).

## Their setup
- Practice software: **ChairSide**. No API. It can write a nightly CSV export at **11pm** to a shared folder:
  `\\HL-SERVER\exports\appts_YYYYMMDD.csv`
- Columns: patient id, first name, last name, mobile, appt date, appt time, provider, location, TXT_OK
- `TXT_OK` is the patient's opt-in to texts. Only text patients with TXT_OK = Y.

## Rules
- HIPAA: the texting vendor has to sign a BAA before any real patient data goes through it.
- Texts carry **only** the first name, the appointment date and time, and the location. No procedure, no provider
  notes, nothing clinical.
- Reminders + a no-show follow-up with a link to rebook.

## Timeline
- Go-live target: **Thursday October 15**.

# Pricing thoughts

No numbers here, just ways of thinking.

## Value pricing, in general
- Price follows what the outcome is worth to the buyer, not hours spent.
- A tool that saves a small team a few hours of repetitive work every week has a value that has little to do with how long it took to write.
- The hardest part is learning what the problem costs them now. Ask.

## Questions to ask
- What happens if nothing changes?
- Who feels the pain: the owner, the manager, or the person doing the clicking?
- What would "done" look like in one sentence?

## Things to be careful about
- Fixed fees punish scope creep unless scope is written down.
- Hourly rewards slow work.
- Discounts teach buyers to ask for them. Trading scope is cleaner.
